**Problem:** How many distinct positive differences can be formed by subtracting one element from another in the set {2, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17}?

**Solution:**

We need to find all values of |a - b| where a, b are distinct elements from the set, then count the distinct results.

The set has 6 elements, so there are 6 × 5 = 30 ordered pairs of distinct elements. By symmetry, each difference d appears twice (once as a - b and once as b - a), so we just need to count distinct positive differences.

**Systematic enumeration:**

- Differences involving 2: |5-2|=3, |7-2|=5, |11-2|=9, |13-2|=11, |17-2|=15
- Differences involving 5: |7-5|=2, |11-5|=6, |13-5|=8, |17-5|=12
- Differences involving 7: |11-7|=4, |13-7|=6, |17-7|=10
- Differences involving 11: |13-11|=2, |17-11|=6
- Differences involving 13: |17-13|=4

**Distinct differences:** {2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15}

**Answer: 11 distinct positive differences**

(Note: 7, 13, 14 are the only gaps under 15, making this a good problem for noticing that not every difference appears.)
